seven_day_host_observations.source: Read-only Monitoring D1 observations joined to festapp/production/festapp-host incident_groups; 0 rows written

critical_containers: Remain uncapped until per-container representative peak and concurrency/recovery checks; admin cap sum plus reserve is not a complete worst-case host allocation. Do not treat per-worker Edge memory as a container cap.
note: Historic host data includes real load/backup windows; new per-container history began after reboot and does not yet cover an equivalent peak. Explicit reserve targets are planning criteria, not enforced reservations.

first_r2_inclusive_backup.note: Entire logical/Storage/runtime/R2 backup, not just R2 overhead; nice=10, existing timer/daemon only. The earlier anon/current sample is not a maximum.

capacity_observation_extension.db_counts: Client connections, active, idle-in-transaction, long transactions; max and reserved connections; collector connection excluded
capacity_observation_extension.edge_counts: Native process-wide live user isolates, including warm workers, plus cumulative received/handled requests
capacity_observation_extension.edge_transport: Numeric allowlist through existing Docker logs and existing minute collector

four_gb_feasibility_screen.interpretation: Screen only: maxima are not simultaneous and are not safe cap recommendations. Under the stated admin ceilings plus OS/backup reserve targets, the remaining allocation is smaller than the sum of already observed working sets. This does not prove production needs a RAM upgrade. A safe enforced all-service budget needs representative peak measurements and an approved capacity or service-lifecycle decision; arbitrary critical caps would not resolve that gap.
